course_details.Overview of class: The Foundations in clinical mental health counseling course, including a Foundations immersion experience, acquaints students with all elements of clinical mental health counseling. Topics include counseling origins, identity, and counseling roles as well as diverse client needs, counseling theories, and counseling practices. This course provides a foundation for further and deeper exploration of these topics throughout the program.

course_details.Overview of class: This course is designed to serve as a clinical and theoretical foundation for the practice of psychodynamic counseling. It emphasizes application to analysis of interpersonal and helping relationships; personality development and dynamics; psychopathology, assessment, and intervention. Requirement: Counseling@Northwestern Students Only.

Jacobs, M. (2024). Psychodynamic Counselling in Action (Counselling in Action Series) (6th ed.). Sage. 9781529682403

course_details.Overview of class:
This course examines contemporary group counseling theories and practices, emphasizing group dynamics, therapeutic processes, ethics, and sociocultural influences. Through lectures, discussion, demonstration, and experiential learning, students develop practical group facilitation skills. A required weekend immersion provides supervised leadership experience, application of theory, increased self-awareness, and deeper understanding of interpersonal and group growth processes within professional counseling contexts and learning environments.

Prerequisite: COUN 416-6 Theories of Counseling.
course_details.Class Materials (Required):
Corey, G., Corey, M., Callanan, P., & Russell, M. (2015). Group techniques. (4th ed.). Cengage. 9780534612696

Corey, G. (2023). Theory and practice of group counseling. (10th ed.). Cengage. 9798214129563

course_details.Overview of class:
This course explores the adaptive, pathological, individual, and family functioning through the life course. Developmental vulnerabilities, transitions, and tasks from a psychodynamic perspective. Emphasis is on development of diagnosis skills using the DSM or ICD formulations. Application will link diagnostic information to current events. Clinical, developmental, and family systems research; onset and dynamics of common psychiatric disorders.

Prerequisite: COUN 423-6 Assessments in Counseling 2 or COUN 426-6 Assessment in Counseling.

course_details.Overview of class:
This course is an introduction to theories and practices of family, marital and couple therapy. The course will examine a) the evolution and foundations of systems; b) classic and contemporary family, marital and couple therapy approaches; c) the impact of cultural/social trends on family and couple life and d) how systems perspectives can be incorporated into the work of one client.

course_details.Overview of class: The course gives students indepth understanding and decision-making skills regarding major ethical and legal issues in the practice of professional counseling. Exploration of of the American Counseling Association (ACA) ethical standards and their application to treatment; review of ethical decision-making models; and major ethical and legal issues in practice. Requirement: Counseling@Northwestern Students Only.

course_details.Overview of class: This course will introduce students to the process of providing counseling from a multi-cultural perspective in diverse society. Students will gain an understanding of how social and cultural identity issues and tensions surface in counseling, how power and privilege may affect therapy alliance and outcomes, the nature of microaggressions. Focus will be on understanding self and clients in cultural context. The counseling profession's value of social justice advocacy for clients will also be examined.
